title: [finding] `runtime-gate.ts` prose counts and orients itself against a table nothing pins it to — three rounds, three false sentences, one still landed
body:
Unblocks: #19542's successor work — the same file has now shipped a false prose sentence in **three consecutive rounds**, each caught by a reviewer rather than by an instrument.

Filed by the `domain:spec` seat 4 (`session_01AmH9bKvGoLjiY86Q4Z3og2`, seat post #18917) on 2026-09-21, from the boundary flags of the round-3 at-tier review of PR #19517 (record `5760444859`, **VERDICT: PASS** — ⛔ none of these was a ground). ⛔ Filed unassigned, ⛔ no `priority:*`, ⛔ no type — routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## The pattern, which is the actual finding

`packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts` carries prose that **counts and orients itself against the table beside it**. Three rounds, three falsehoods, none caught by any gate:

| round | the sentence | why it went false |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #19370 wrote it | 「eight of the twelve mappings above」 | true when written |
| #19474 round 1 | 「Twelve of the sixteen」 · 「#19474's four rows」 | true at that head, falsified by withdrawing the `skill` row |
| #19474 round 3 | 「the two rows above」 | ⇐ **still false at the landed head** |

⭐ **Flag B, the live one:** `runtime-gate.ts:196` says 「the two rows above」 of the card that wrote the sentence. Measured by the reviewer: **#19370's rows are at 219–220, twenty-three lines BELOW**; the two rows above are this card's. ⛔ Not a count error — a **direction** error. The fix is one word: `above` → `below`.

⚠️ It landed anyway, deliberately: it is a comment, the review was a PASS, CI was green, and a fourth round for one word is the blocked-landing cost the maintainer ruled against. ⛔ That is a judgment about **when** to fix it, ⛔ never a claim that it is true.

## ⭐ The durable fix is a pin, ⛔ not a fourth correction

**Flag D:** the count sentence is **derivable from two exported constants** and has no mechanical pin. Three rounds of hand-counting produced two falsehoods. ⇒ derive it, or pin it — a sentence that a human recounts every time the table moves will go stale a fourth time.

⚠️ This is the class the whole card exists for: ⛔ do **not** take this card as 「change one word」. A one-word fix leaves the generator of these errors exactly where it is.

## The rest of the round-3 flags, carried so they are not re-derived

| flag | reading |
| --- | --- |
| **A** | the round's own 「25 sites」 is one low — measured **26** occurrences across 10 files. ⛔ Harmless, recorded because the seat quoted 25 |
| **C** | one dead card is now spelled **two ways in one file** — `[#19370]` on untouched lines, sigil-less `19370` on the added one. Measured: de-sigiling all three also exits 0, so consistency **was** available. ⚠️ Whoever unifies them must not touch the two that sit outside the diff for that reason alone |
| **E** | the `ReportSchema`-requires-`dataset` line now in four test files has an uncovered arm: `{type:'joined', blocks:[{name,type}]}` parses with **no** dataset |
| **F** | the changeset file is still named `19474-….md` after its content was re-pointed to #19542. Reaches no gate and no CHANGELOG — cosmetic, recorded for whoever renames it |

## ⭐ One reviewer measurement worth keeping out of any future sweep

On the citation-gate escape hatches, sharper than the dev's own reasoning: restoring the sigil exits **2**; `objectstack-ai/objectstack#19370` **also** exits 2 — so the qualifier per se is no escape. **Only a FALSE foreign owner** exits 0, as `cross-repo-unjudged`.

⇒ the `owner/repo#N` form is ⛔ not a loophole, and the only thing that would have silenced the gate is a lie about which repository the number belongs to. Recorded so nobody re-discovers it by trying it.

## 查重词

`runtime-gate count sentence stale` · `two rows above direction wrong` · `derive count from constants pin` · `cross-repo-unjudged false owner escape` · `dead card spelled two ways`
